source.title: LeXFiles and LegalLAMA: Facilitating English Multinational Legal Language Model Development
source.authors: Ilias Chalkidis; Nicolas Garneau; Catalina Goanta; D. Katz; Anders Søgaard

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares downstream task scores across differently sized pretrained models, a different measure and setting from the original scaling-law measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports MLM token accuracy, not held-out cross-entropy loss, so those results do not measure V1. It does not fit scaling laws or test extrapolation or compute-optimal allocations. Its downstream classification scores and discussion of model capacity bear on V6. Scaling-law papers cited in the text are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: A legal-NLP resource paper, not a scaling study. It compares base (124M) and large (355M) versions of RoBERTa and LexLM on six fine-tuned legal tasks (Table 5) and states that capacity correlates with downstream performance. That is a two-point size comparison in a new setting (legal encoders, one-epoch fine-tuning) bearing on V6. There is no loss measurement, curve fit or extrapolation, so it is T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that downstream performance is driven mainly by model size and by prior legal knowledge. For upstream and probing, pretraining corpus has a much larger effect than size, though larger models trained on similar corpora do better overall. They also note that the link between legal knowledge and downstream scores is mixed for base models and holds only among large models.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates legal encoder models on MLM accuracy, probing benchmarks, and fine-tuned legal classification tasks; it does not use the original scaling-law loss-fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream results vary with task and pretraining corpus; the authors note task exceptions to the overall model-capacity trend.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a family, larger models get higher upstream MLM accuracy (RoBERTa 70.1 to 73.8, LexLM 78.7 to 81.8, Table 3) and higher probing MRR. The authors say pretraining corpus matters much more than size: LegalBERT-base beats RoBERTa-L.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-specific masked-LM accuracy depends more on pretraining corpus than on model size at the 100-350M scale.

fits_no_version.finding: For base models, upstream/probing legal knowledge does not correlate with downstream scores; for large models it does (Section 4.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining-metric (MLM accuracy) predictiveness of downstream performance depends on model size regime.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The downstream comparison is limited to encoder-only models up to approximately 350M parameters and six legal tasks. Models differ in pretraining corpora and setups, and the downstream fine-tuning uses only one epoch. No scaling-law fits, held-out cross-entropy results, or uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 also reports task-level macro-F1 for the six tasks; these task-specific macro-F1 entries were not extracted under the 60-row cap. The task-level micro-F1 results and both aggregate metrics were retained.

untested.parts: No held-out cross-entropy loss. Only MLM accuracy is reported, with no scaling fit.
No controlled shape comparison at fixed parameters.
No power-law form in fine-tuning or transfer. Only two sizes per family.
No fitted or predictive curve (only two sizes, encoder-only, up to about 355M). No relation to pretraining loss. Behaviour under longer fine-tuning is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope label over all task rows was wrong: same-family task-level comparisons uniformly favour the larger model. The limits come from small gains on some tasks and from confounded cross-family comparisons. The evidence is weak: two sizes, single-epoch fine-tuning, and no uncertainty reported. Tranche changed from T2 to T3.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from fits on small runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Scaling laws in other modalities or training regimes.
No relationship to pretraining loss is tested; the results cover a limited set of encoder models and legal downstream tasks, not a fitted or broadly predictive scale curve.
No comparison of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Same-family size comparisons (RoBERTa-B to L, LexLM-B to L), legal tasks, one-epoch fine-tuning
relationships.reason: The larger model beats the base model on all 6 tasks and both averages in both families (R3, R4, R13, R14, R16, R21, R23, R28, R35, R37, R42, R44, R49, R51, R56).
relationships.display_finding: The larger variant outperformed the base variant on all six tasks and both averages within each family.

relationships.condition: Size of the gain varies by task. Across model families with different pretraining, size does not predict rank.
relationships.reason: The RoBERTa CNLI gain is only +1.2 (R30), against about +29 on EURLEX (R51). LegalBERT (110M) beats the 340-355M models on CNLI and CaseHOLD (R31, R45 vs R30, R33, R44, R47), per the paper's stated 2/6 exceptions.
relationships.display_finding: RoBERTa gained only 1.2 points on CNLI versus about 29 on EURLEX, while LegalBERT 110M outperformed 340–355M models on CNLI and CaseHOLD.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Overall averages for the RoBERTa Base/Large and LexLM Base/Large pairs
reader_labels.reason: The reported averages are higher for the larger variant in both paired model families and both metrics (R1–R4, R11–R14). The paper also states that capacity strongly correlates with overall downstream performance.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Individual downstream tasks and comparisons across different pretraining setups
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports mixed task-level outcomes and says LegalBERT outperforms larger models in 2/6 tasks; pretraining setup also affects results, so these comparisons do not establish a general predictive scale relationship (R15–R56).
